summary: Schedule-sensitive Confluence space export with conditional Slack digest gateway and scoped service-account
description: Compliance has requested an automated, auditable export pipeline for a single high-sensitivity Confluence space (space key: HR-SENSITIVE). Requirements: weekly full-space export (PDF+XML) stored encrypted in customer-s3-bucket, retention snapshot naming by ISO date, and an approval-gated Slack digest posted only to pre-approved #compliance-archive channel after export completes. Exports must run under a scoped service account (no broad Confluence admin privileges), record audit events, and attach the S3 object URI to the Jira ticket for review. The automation should include a kill-switch and backoff on export failures and must preserve existing page attachments and permissions. Security requires KMS encryption and an auditable access log. Please propose implementation that minimizes Confluence REST rate impacts and follows runbook compliance/export-standard-3.
steps_to_reproduce: (This is an implementation request rather than a user bug. Testing plan to validate delivery:) 1) Create a scoped service-account in Atlassian with read/export permissions restricted to HR-SENSITIVE. 2) Implement a scheduled exporter job (AWS Lambda or k8s cron) that uses the Confluence export endpoint, streams export to S3 with server-side KMS encryption, and emits CloudTrail/Access logs. 3) On success, post a hashed digest summary to #compliance-archive with an approval button that triggers signed-download links. 4) On failure, escalate to #infra-support and create a blocking ticket. 5) Validate end-to-end in staging (staging.space: HR-SENSITIVE-STG) before scheduling weekly job in prod. 6) Document runbook and add health check to Redwood Console alerts.
